items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「歳とり膳」は、大晦日の夜に家族そろっていただく宮崎の正月料理。タイや塩イワシなど縁起物とされる「歳とり魚」に、煮しめ、白和え、煮豆、なます、おこわ、吸い物などが並ぶ。沿岸部ではタイ、山間部では塩イワシが使われることが多いという。一年の無事を歳神様に感謝しながらいただく、ハレの膳という。高膳に盛られた料理を家族で囲む、年に一度の特別な食卓でもある。

## どう作るのか
地域や家庭によって使う具材や内容はさまざまだが、歳とり魚を中心に、根菜を炊き合わせた煮しめや、豆腐を使った白和え、酢の物のなますなどを一通りそろえる。大晦日に用意したものを元旦にもいただき、三が日はその残りを食べることが多いという。各家庭で味付けや盛り付けに個性が出るのも特徴という。歳神様にお供えしたものと同じ料理を家族もいただくのが習わしという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
かつて旧暦を使っていたころ、一日は日没後にはじまるとされ、大晦日の夕方からすでに新年として祝われていたと伝わる。数え年で歳を数えていた時代、お正月を迎えることは家族そろって歳を一つ重ねる喜びの日でもあったという。輸送手段が限られていた昔、魚は貴重な食材でありごちそうだったとされ、歳神様を迎える特別な膳として大切に受け継がれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Toshitori-zen is a New Year's Eve meal shared by the family in Miyazaki. It centers on an auspicious "year-taking fish," typically sea bream along the coast or salted sardine in the mountains, alongside simmered vegetables, tofu-dressed greens, simmered beans, a vinegared salad, glutinous rice, and a clear soup. It's a formal meal eaten in gratitude to the year's guardian deity for a year passed safely.

## How it's made
The exact dishes vary by region and household, but the meal typically centers on the year-taking fish alongside root vegetables simmered together, tofu-dressed greens, and a vinegared vegetable salad. What's prepared on New Year's Eve is also eaten on New Year's Day, and the leftovers often carry through the first three days of the year. Seasoning and presentation are said to differ from one household to the next.

## Why it took this shape
Under the old lunar calendar, a day was reportedly considered to begin at nightfall, so New Year's Eve evening was already treated as the start of the new year. In an era when age was counted by the calendar year rather than the birthday, reaching the New Year meant the whole family gained a year together, a moment of shared celebration. With transport limited in the past, fish was a precious ingredient and a genuine treat, and this meal is said to have been passed down as a special way to welcome the new year's deity.

sources.title: 歳とり膳 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「煮しめ」は、しいたけや里芋、たけのこ、こんにゃく、厚揚げなどを、煮汁が残らないようじっくり時間をかけて煮つめた宮崎県内全域の料理。地域によって地鶏やいりこ、干しアジ、昆布など出汁の素材が異なり、具材にも県北部の干したけのこ、県央部の鶏肉など土地ごとの個性があるという。ふっくらと味の染みた具材を一つひとつ味わえる一皿という。

## どう作るのか
しいたけ、里芋、たけのこ、こんにゃく、ごぼう、ぜんまいなどを、しょうゆやみりん、砂糖といった調味料とともに、煮汁が残らなくなるまでじっくり煮つめる。火を止めたあとも余熱でしっかり味を含ませるのがポイントという。季節の野菜を加えることも多く、地域や家庭ごとに具材の組み合わせが異なるという。出汁をとる素材も地鶏やいりこ、昆布などさまざまという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
煮汁が残らないよう煮つめることを「煮しめる」ということから、この名がついたと伝わる。もともとは祝い事や冠婚葬祭に欠かせない料理で、お正月のおせちに詰められたり、高千穂町の神楽奉納で振る舞われたりしてきたという。それぞれの具材に願いが込められ、一緒に煮ることで家族が末永く仲良くありますようにという意味も込められていると伝わる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Nishime, found across Miyazaki, simmers shiitake, taro, bamboo shoot, konjac, and deep-fried tofu slowly until the cooking liquid nearly disappears. The broth base varies by area, from free-range chicken and dried sardine to dried horse mackerel or kombu, and the choice of ingredients also differs by region, such as dried bamboo shoot and shiitake in the north or chicken in the central area, so each version has its own local flavor, with every ingredient soaking up the seasoning fully.

## How it's made
Shiitake, taro, bamboo shoot, konjac, burdock, and flowering fern are simmered slowly together with soy sauce, mirin, and sugar until almost no liquid remains. Letting the pot sit in its residual heat after cooking is said to help the flavor soak in further. Seasonal vegetables are often added, and the combination of ingredients varies from region to region and household to household.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to take its name from the verb "nishimeru," meaning to simmer down until the liquid is gone. Originally it was considered essential for celebrations and ceremonial occasions, and it's said to have been packed into New Year's osechi boxes or served during the all-night kagura dance offerings in Takachiho. Each ingredient reportedly carries its own meaning, and simmering them together is said to express a wish for the family to stay close and thrive for years to come.

sources.title: 煮しめ 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「魚ずし」は、サバやアジ、イワシなどを姿のまま塩と酢でしめてつくる宮崎県北沿岸部のなれずし。江戸時代、天領地だった門川町の名物として知られてきたという。塩でしっかりしめた魚を酢に漬けこみ、中まで赤みが残らないようにするのが特徴で、酢の風味と魚の旨みが凝縮された一品という。サバやアジのほか、イワシやカマスを使うこともあるという。

## どう作るのか
サバやアジは背開きに、イワシは腹開きにして塩でしっかりしめる。そのあと酢に漬けこみ、中まで酢でしめるため一晩置くこともあるという。川南町の通浜では、レンコダイや小アジなどとれたての小魚を三枚におろして塩をふり酢に漬け、その間にすし飯を用意する。酢と砂糖を合わせた合わせ酢を炊きたてのごはんに混ぜてゆっくり冷まし、丸めたごはんに魚をのせていただくという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
四国の郷土ずし・姿ずしが海を渡って宮崎県沿岸部に伝わったという説があり、かつては冬祭りに欠かせないごちそうだったと伝わる。天領地だった門川町では、やってくる役人にふるまう一品として親しまれたともいわれる。日向灘でとれた新鮮な魚を行商人が届けてくれたことから、家庭でも手軽につくられる料理として根づいていったという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Sakana-zushi is a preserved sushi from the northern coast of Miyazaki, made by curing whole mackerel, horse mackerel, or sardine in salt and vinegar. It's known as a specialty of Kadogawa, once a shogunate-administered territory during the Edo period. The fish is firmly salted, then marinated in vinegar until no pink shows through to the center, giving the dish a concentrated tang and rich fish flavor.

## How it's made
Mackerel and horse mackerel are butterflied open from the back, sardine from the belly, and all are firmly salted. They are then marinated in vinegar, sometimes overnight, until fully cured through. In the Toriehama area of Kawaminami, freshly caught small fish such as crimson sea bream or young horse mackerel are filleted, salted, and marinated in vinegar while the sushi rice is prepared separately: a vinegar-sugar mixture is folded into hot rice and left to cool slowly before being shaped by hand and topped with the cured fish.

## Why it took this shape
One account holds that this style of sushi crossed the sea from a similar dish in Shikoku and took root along Miyazaki's coast, and it's said to have once been an essential treat at winter festivals. In Kadogawa, a shogunate territory at the time, it reportedly became a favorite dish served to visiting officials. With traveling fish sellers bringing in fresh catch from the Hyuga Sea, it's said to have taken hold as something households could put together easily at home as well.

sources.title: 魚ずし 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
延岡市に伝わる「ふたたびだんご」は、もち粉と小麦粉を合わせた生地によもぎを練りこみ、甘さ控えめのあんを包んできな粉をまぶしただんご。生地を一度こねてから蒸し、再びついてつくることからこの名がついたという。よもぎの若草色が目にも鮮やかで、ふわっとやわらかな食感が持ち味という。だんご粉には「やわみ」と呼ばれる専用の粉が使われることもあるという。

## どう作るのか
もち粉と小麦粉を6対4ほどの割合で合わせ、水を加えて耳たぶほどのやわらかさになるまでこねる。川原で摘んだよもぎの新芽を加えて蒸し、再び生地をつくのが「ふたたびだんご」ならではの工程という。ゆでたよもぎをすり鉢でつきつぶし、塩少々を加えて色を全体にまわしたら、あんを包んで丸め、きな粉をまぶして仕上げる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
通常のだんごづくりは生地をこねる作業が一度だが、「ふたたびだんご」ははじめにこねた生地をよもぎとともに蒸し、再びついてつくることから、この名がついたと伝わる。二度手間をかけることで、とてもやわらかくふわっとした食感の生地に仕上がるという。よもぎは古くから薬草としても使われ、春先にやわらかい若葉が出るこの時期につくられるようになったという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Futatabi-dango, from Nobeoka, is a dumpling made from a dough of glutinous and wheat flour kneaded with mugwort, wrapped around a lightly sweetened bean paste, and dusted with kinako soybean flour. It's said to take its name from being kneaded, steamed, and then pounded a second time. The vivid green of the mugwort is striking to look at, and its softness, with a light, springy chew, is the dumpling's signature trait.

## How it's made
Glutinous rice flour and wheat flour are combined at roughly a six-to-four ratio, mixed with water, and kneaded until soft as an earlobe. Young mugwort shoots picked along the riverbank are worked in, and the dough is steamed and then pounded a second time, the step that gives this dumpling its name. The boiled mugwort is pounded in a mortar with a little salt until its color spreads evenly through the dough, which is then wrapped around bean paste, rolled into balls, and dusted with kinako.

## Why it took this shape
A typical dumpling dough is kneaded only once, but this one is kneaded, steamed together with mugwort, and then pounded a second time, which is said to be the origin of its name, meaning "dumpling done twice." That extra round of work is said to give the dough its notably soft, springy texture. Mugwort has long been used as an herbal remedy, and this dumpling is said to have become a seasonal treat made when tender new mugwort leaves appear in early spring.

sources.title: ふたたびだんご 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「メヒカリの唐揚げ」は、延岡市沖の日向灘でとれる小魚メヒカリを丸ごと揚げた料理。大きく青く光る目が特徴で、この名がついたという。正式な和名は「アオメエソ」。骨がやわらかい魚のため、から揚げにすると骨を気にせず丸ごと食べられ、淡白な白身とふんわりした食感を楽しめるという。体長5〜15cmほどの小さな魚で、丸ごと一尾が一口サイズにおさまるのも魅力という。

## どう作るのか
頭を切り落とし、内臓とうろこを取って水ですすぎ、水気をきる。塩こしょうをふって小麦粉か片栗粉をまぶし、180℃に熱した油で揚げる。骨まで丸ごと食べられるのが魅力で、お酒の肴にもよく合うという。唐揚げのほか、南蛮漬けや天ぷら、塩焼きにされることもあり、新鮮なものは刺身でも味わえるという。産卵期の5〜6月を除きほぼ通年出まわるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
かつては底引き網漁でとれる雑魚として扱われ、漁師のまかない飯や養殖用のエサに使われていたと伝わる。見た目に反した淡白な白身とふんわりした食感を知ってもらおうと、延岡市の料理人が試行錯誤を重ねて調理法を編み出し、次第に注目されるようになったという。産卵期を除くほぼ通年水揚げされ、最盛期を心待ちにする地元の人も多いという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Mehikari no karaage deep-fries mehikari, a small fish caught in the Hyuga Sea off Nobeoka, whole. Its name is said to come from its large, striking blue eyes. The fish's formal Japanese name is "aomeeso." Because its bones are soft, deep-frying lets the whole fish be eaten without worrying about them, letting diners enjoy its mild white flesh and light, airy texture.

## How it's made
The head is cut off, the innards and scales removed, and the fish rinsed and drained. It's seasoned with salt and pepper, dusted with wheat flour or potato starch, and deep-fried in oil heated to about 180°C. Being able to eat it bones and all is part of its appeal, and it pairs well with sake. Beyond deep-frying, it's also prepared as nanban-zuke marinade, tempura, or salt-grilled, and the freshest catch is sometimes served raw as sashimi.

## Why it took this shape
The fish was once treated as bycatch from deep-sea shrimp trawling, reportedly eaten by fishermen themselves or used as feed for farmed fish. Chefs in Nobeoka are said to have experimented with ways to showcase its mild flesh and light texture, which belied its plain appearance, and the fish gradually gained wider attention as a result. It's landed nearly year-round outside the spawning season, and many locals reportedly look forward to the peak season each year.

sources.title: めひかりの唐揚げ 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
椎葉村に伝わる「菜豆腐」は、豆腐のなかに季節の花や青菜を混ぜこんだ料理。春は菜の花や山藤の花、三つ葉、秋から春にかけては「平家かぶ」と呼ばれる青菜が使われるという。花や青菜の彩りと香りが豆腐にほんのりと移り、見た目にも華やかな一品という。なかでも藤の花を使った豆腐は、他ではあまり見られない珍しいものという。

## どう作るのか
大豆とにがりからつくる豆腐に、ゆでた青菜や季節の花を混ぜこんで固める。からし菜を入れてぴりっとした風味にしたり、桜や山椒の葉、大根の葉を干したものを用いたりするほか、近年は大根や人参、里芋、青じそ、ほうれん草など身近な季節野菜も使われるという。水につけずに切り分け、しょうゆや練り味噌、柚子味噌をつけてそのまま食べる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
椎葉村は平家の落人伝説が残る山間の村で、日常の言葉にも上方言葉の名残があり、京料理を思わせる食文化が伝わってきたとされる。やせた土地でも育つ「平家かぶ」を混ぜこむことで、貴重な大豆を節約しながら豆腐の量を増やす工夫が生まれたと伝わる。半世紀ほど前まで豆腐は日常のごちそうであり、祝い事から法事まで幅広い場で食べられてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Nadoufu, handed down in Shiiba village, mixes seasonal flowers or greens into tofu. Rapeseed blossoms, wisteria flowers, or mitsuba greens go in during spring, while a local green called "heike-kabu" is used from autumn through spring. The color and aroma of the flowers or greens carry gently into the tofu, making for a dish as striking to look at as it is to eat; the wisteria-flower version in particular is said to be a rare kind of tofu seen almost nowhere else.

## How it's made
Tofu made from soybeans and nigari is mixed with boiled greens or seasonal flowers before it sets. Some versions use spicy mustard greens for a sharp bite, or dried sakura, sansho, or daikon leaves, while more recent recipes use everyday seasonal vegetables such as daikon, carrot, taro, shiso, or spinach. It's cut into pieces without soaking in water and eaten as is, dipped in soy sauce, sweet miso paste, or yuzu miso.

## Why it took this shape
Shiiba is a mountain village associated with legends of Heike clan refugees, and traces of old Kyoto dialect reportedly survive in everyday speech there, said to have shaped a food culture reminiscent of Kyoto cuisine. Mixing in heike-kabu, a green that grows even in poor soil, is said to have let households stretch precious soybeans while bulking up the tofu. Until about half a century ago, tofu was an everyday treat, and this dish is said to have been served on occasions ranging from celebrations to memorial services.

sources.title: 菜豆腐 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
高千穂町に伝わる「かっぽ鶏」は、竹筒を器にして地鶏や野菜を蒸し焼きにする料理。竹の節と節の間をくり抜いて器にすることから、この地方の方言で竹を指す「かっぽ」の名がついたという。竹から出る香りとエキスが具材にまろやかな風味を加え、器に使う竹によっても味わいが変わるという。竹をそのまま器にする野趣あふれる見た目も、この料理ならではの持ち味という。

## どう作るのか
竹の節と節の間の一部をくり抜き、下味をつけた鶏肉や野菜を詰める。くり抜いた部分をふたのようにかぶせ、竹ごと火にかけると、具材が竹の中で蒸されるようにじっくりと熱が通るという。竹から出る香りとエキスが加わりまろやかな味わいになるため、エキスが出やすい1年ものの若い青竹が良いとされる。味付けや具材に決まりはなく、家庭ごとに秘伝のたれがあるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
竹に水を注ぐと「かっぽかっぽ」という音がすることが名の由来といわれる。もともとは山林の仕事や刈干し切りの合間に、谷川の水をくんで竹筒で温め、お茶を飲んだことがはじまりと伝わる。竹が豊富な高千穂町ならではの知恵として、地元でとれる地鶏や野菜を竹筒に詰めて蒸し焼きにする調理法が根づいていったという。焼酎を竹筒で燗した「かっぽ酒」とともに味わう習わしもあると伝わる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Kappo-dori, handed down in Takachiho, steams free-range chicken and vegetables inside a bamboo tube. It's named after "kappo," the local dialect word for bamboo, since the dish is cooked in a section of bamboo hollowed out between its joints. The aroma and natural moisture released from the bamboo give the ingredients a mellow flavor, one that reportedly varies depending on the bamboo used.

## How it's made
A section between two bamboo joints is hollowed out and packed with pre-seasoned chicken and vegetables. The hollowed piece is set back on top like a lid, and the whole tube is set over a fire, letting the heat work through slowly as the ingredients steam inside. The aroma and natural moisture from the bamboo give the dish its mellow flavor, and young, one-year-old green bamboo is said to be best since it releases the most of that flavor. There's no fixed recipe for the seasoning or ingredients, and many households are said to keep their own secret sauce.

## Why it took this shape
The name is said to come from the "kappo kappo" sound water makes when poured into a bamboo tube. It's said to have originated with workers pouring water from a mountain stream into a bamboo tube to warm and brew tea during breaks from forestry work or grass cutting. Making the most of Takachiho's abundant bamboo, packing local free-range chicken and vegetables into a tube and steaming them over a fire is said to have taken hold as a resourceful local method.

sources.title: かっぽ鶏 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
椎葉村に伝わる「そまげ」は、煮干しの出汁を効かせた野菜入りの汁にそば粉を混ぜてつくる、そばがきに似た料理。「そま」はそば、「げ」はおかゆを意味するという。大根や人参、ねぎなど淡白な野菜の味わいに、そば粉のとろみと香ばしさが加わり、体の温まる素朴な味わいという。地域によってはさつまいもとそば粉を合わせる似た料理も伝わっている。

## どう作るのか
いりこで出汁をとり、千切りにした野菜を塩やしょうゆで味付けしながら煮る。煮立ったところへそば粉を混ぜ込み、だんご状にまとめる。固くなったら小さく切って囲炉裏で焼いて食べることもあったという。寒い日によくつくられ、体を芯から温める食べ方として親しまれてきたという。仕上がりのとろみ加減は、そば粉を加えるタイミングで調整できるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
やせ地や涼しい山地に適したそばは、古くから米の代用として栽培されてきたとされる。収穫したそばの実を石臼でひいて粉にし、淡白な山菜や野菜の味を、油や薬味で濃厚に仕立てるための工夫として「そまげ」が生まれたと伝わる。お米が貴重だった時代、代用食として寒い日に食べられ、椎葉村の暮らしに深く根づいていったという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Somage, from Shiiba village, is a buckwheat dish similar to sobagaki dumplings, made by stirring buckwheat flour into a vegetable soup flavored with dried sardine dashi. "Soma" refers to buckwheat and "ge" to porridge in the local dialect. The plain flavor of daikon, carrot, and scallion meets the thick, nutty character of buckwheat flour for a simple, warming dish.

## How it's made
Dashi is made from dried sardine, and shredded vegetables are simmered in it, seasoned with salt or soy sauce. Once it comes to a boil, buckwheat flour is stirred in and gathered into dumpling-like lumps. If it hardens, it can be cut into small pieces and grilled over an open hearth. It was often made on cold days, valued as a way to warm the body from within.

## Why it took this shape
Buckwheat, suited to poor soil and cool mountain terrain, is said to have long been grown as a substitute for rice. The harvested grain was ground into flour with a stone mill, and somage is said to have developed as a way to turn the plain flavor of mountain vegetables into something richer with the help of oil and seasoning. In an era when rice was scarce, it's said to have served as a substitute food eaten on cold days, taking root deeply in the everyday life of Shiiba village.

sources.title: そまげ 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
椎葉村に伝わる「稗ずーしー」は、猪の骨付き肉を湯がいたスープに米や稗、内臓肉、野菜を入れて炊きあげる雑炊。雑炊のことを地元で「ずし」と呼ぶことから、この名がついたという。稗は縄文以前から食べられてきたとされる雑穀で、外皮が固く長期保存がきき、体を温める働きがあるとされる。猪の出汁がしみた稗の風味豊かな一杯という。

## どう作るのか
精白した稗を糠を流す程度に軽く洗い、あらかじめとっておいた猪のだし汁に入れる。トロ火にかけて約2時間、アクをすくい取りながらじっくり煮る。味付けは塩のみがよいとされる。猪をさばいた際には、身や骨を大鍋で水炊きしてアクを取り、そこに稗を加えて雑炊にし、村中でふるまうこともあったという。少量ずつ鍋に取り分け、だし汁で増やして温め直すこともあったと伝わる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
お米が貴重だった時代、日々の主食は「稗めし」が中心で、お米は正月や祭事のためにとっておかれたとされる。狩猟が盛んな椎葉村では、猪の肉を余さず活かす知恵として、骨付き肉の出汁に稗を合わせる雑炊が根づいたと伝わる。他の穀物と比べて腹持ちが良く、ごはんが少ないときや寒い日の夕食として、長い冬を乗り切る栄養源になったという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Hie-zushii, handed down in Shiiba village, is a rice porridge made by simmering rice, millet, wild boar innards, and vegetables in a broth boiled from bone-in wild boar meat. The dish is named after "zushi," a local word for porridge. Millet, said to have been eaten since before the Jomon period, has a tough hull that keeps well over long storage and is said to help warm the body, giving this dish a rich flavor carried by the wild boar broth.

## How it's made
Polished millet is rinsed lightly, just enough to wash off the bran, then added to a broth made ahead of time from wild boar bones. It's simmered over low heat for about two hours, skimming off the scum as it cooks. Salt alone is said to be the best seasoning. When a boar was hunted and dressed, the meat and bones were simmered in a large pot, the scum skimmed off, and millet added to make a porridge sometimes shared with the whole village.

## Why it took this shape
In an era when rice was precious, the everyday staple was reportedly a millet-based dish, with rice set aside for New Year's and festivals. In Shiiba village, known for its hunting tradition, using every part of a hunted boar is said to have led to this porridge, simmering millet in bone broth. Said to be more filling than other grains, it served as a source of nutrition on cold evenings or when rice ran short, helping households get through the long winter.

sources.title: 稗ずーしー 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「とうきびめし」は、高千穂地方に伝わる麦飯と並ぶ主食の一つ。乾燥させたとうもろこし（とうきび）を踏臼でひき割りにし、米に混ぜて炊きあげる。とうきびの香ばしい風味と彩りが加わり、米だけのごはんとはひと味違う食べ応えになるという。「とうきびごはん」とも呼ばれ、寒風にさらして乾燥させたとうきびならではの旨味も感じられる一品という。

## どう作るのか
米に1〜2割ほどのとうきびを混ぜ、水加減を少し多めにして塩を加えて炊く。最初から米と一緒に炊く方法と、とうきびをあらかじめゆがいておいてから米に加える方法があるという。炊きたてはそのまま食べるが、冷えると味が落ちるため、昼夜の分は熱いうちににぎり飯にしておき、日常は囲炉裏で焼いて食べていたと伝わる。

## なぜこの形になったのか
夏に畑や焼畑にとうきびの種を播き、秋の中頃に収穫したものを馬小屋の軒下に掛けて寒風にさらし、じっくり乾燥させて旨味を蓄えたとされる。米が貴重だった時代、割ったとうきびで米のかさを増やし、人々の空腹を満たす知恵として広まったと伝わる。一年中麦飯が続くなかで、とうきびめしの香りと彩りが食卓に変化をもたらしていたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Toukibi-meshi is a staple food from the Takachiho region, served alongside barley rice. Dried corn kernels, cracked with a foot-powered mill, are mixed into rice and cooked together. The corn's nutty aroma and color give the rice a heartier character than plain rice alone, and the dish is also known as "toukibi gohan."

## How it's made
Rice is mixed with corn at roughly ten to twenty percent of the volume, cooked with a bit more water than usual and a pinch of salt. Some cook the corn together with the rice from the start, while others parboil the corn first and add it in afterward. It's best eaten fresh, since the flavor fades once it cools, so portions for midday and evening were reportedly shaped into rice balls while still hot, and everyday portions were often grilled over an open hearth.

## Why it took this shape
Corn was reportedly sown in fields or on cleared mountain plots in summer, harvested by mid-autumn, then hung under the eaves of a stable and left to dry slowly in the cold mountain wind, said to concentrate its flavor. In an era when rice was scarce, mixing in cracked corn is said to have stretched the rice supply and helped fill people's stomachs, a practical solution that spread through the region. Amid a diet otherwise dominated by barley rice year-round, this dish's aroma and color are said to have brought a welcome change to the table.

sources.title: とうきびめし 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「冷や汁」は、焼いてすった味噌に出汁を合わせた冷たい汁を、熱い麦飯にかけていただく宮崎県央地方の料理。タイやアジを素焼きにしてほぐした身をすりこんだものが贅沢版で、煮干しを使う場合もあるという。小口切りのきゅうりや青じそ、みょうがを添え、冷たい汁と温かいごはんの対比を楽しむ一品という。日向灘でとれる新鮮な魚介と太陽の恵みを受けた野菜を生かした食べ方でもある。

## どう作るのか
タイやアジを素焼きにして身をほぐし、骨をていねいに取り除く。すり鉢で白ごまをすり、ほぐした魚の身と味噌を合わせてすり鉢の内側に塗りつけ、炭火の上にさかさまに伏せて表面に焦げめがつくまで炙る。焼いた味噌をだし汁でとき、味噌汁より濃いめに仕立てて冷やす。小口切りのきゅうりをのせ、熱々の麦飯にかけていただくという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
暑く湿気の多い宮崎の気候のなかで、農民が夏の重労働の合間に、麦飯に生味噌をのせて水をかけて食べていたことがはじまりと伝わる。山地の多い宮崎県では、藩政時代には米が非常に貴重だったとされ、麦飯が日常の主食だったという。時間や食欲がないときでも手早く栄養と体力を補える生活の知恵として、夏の農作業を支える一杯になったと伝わる。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Hiyajiru, from central Miyazaki, is a cold soup of grilled, mashed miso mixed into dashi and poured over hot barley rice. In its richer version, grilled and flaked sea bream or horse mackerel is worked into the miso, though dried sardine sometimes stands in. Sliced cucumber, shiso, and myoga are added on top, playing the cold soup against the hot rice.

## How it's made
Sea bream or horse mackerel is grilled plain and flaked, the bones carefully removed. White sesame is ground in a mortar, mixed with the flaked fish and miso, and the paste is spread inside the mortar, then held upside down over charcoal embers until its surface is lightly charred. The toasted miso is thinned with dashi into a soup thicker than ordinary miso soup, then chilled. Sliced cucumber is added on top, and the cold soup is poured over hot barley rice to finish.

## Why it took this shape
In Miyazaki's hot, humid climate, this dish is said to have started with farmers topping barley rice with raw miso and water during breaks from heavy summer labor. In the mountainous parts of Miyazaki, rice was reportedly a precious commodity under the old domain system, with barley rice serving as the everyday staple. As a way to get quick nutrition and recover strength even without much time or appetite, it's said to have become an essential dish supporting farmers through the summer harvest.

sources.title: 冷や汁 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「ぬた芋」は、ゆでた里芋にすりごま、味噌、砂糖、みりんなどを合わせた和え衣をからめる宮崎県央地方の料理。里芋の角がとれてとろみが増すのが特徴で、一部をすりつぶして合わせるとさらに豊かなとろみと粘りが出るという。ホクホクとした里芋に、ごまと味噌の風味、ほどよい甘みがからむ素朴な味わいという。秋にとれる小さめの里芋がよく使われるという。

## どう作るのか
里芋を皮ごとやわらかくなるまでゆで、皮をむいて食べやすい大きさに切る。すりごま、味噌、砂糖、みりんなどを合わせた調味料で和えれば出来上がりという。和えているうちに里芋の角がとれ、とろみが増していくのがこの料理らしいところで、一部をすりつぶして混ぜるとより豊かな粘りが生まれるという。お酒のつまみにも、子どものおやつにもなる万能な一品という。

## なぜこの形になったのか
里芋の生産量が全国でも上位に位置する宮崎県では、昔から里芋を使った料理が親しまれてきたとされる。秋にとれる小さめの里芋を無駄なく使う工夫として「ぬた芋」が生まれたと伝わる。名の由来ははっきりしないが、和えるときにぬたぬたすることから、または酢味噌和えの「ぬた」と同様、ぬめりを沼田に見立てたことからともいわれている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Nutaimo, from central Miyazaki, coats boiled taro in a dressing of ground sesame, miso, sugar, and mirin. As it's mixed, the taro's edges soften into a thicker, stickier texture, and mashing part of the taro into the dressing makes it richer still. The soft, starchy taro carries the flavor of sesame and miso with a gentle sweetness, in a simple, homey dish.

## How it's made
Taro is boiled in its skin until soft, then peeled and cut into bite-sized pieces. It's tossed with a dressing of ground sesame, miso, sugar, and mirin, and that's it. As the taro is mixed with the dressing, its edges round off and the dish grows thicker and stickier, a defining trait of this dish, and mashing part of the taro into the mix adds even more body.

## Why it took this shape
Miyazaki, among the leading producers of taro in the country, is said to have long favored dishes built around it. Nutaimo is said to have developed as a way to make good use of the small taro corms harvested in autumn. Its name isn't clearly settled, but one account ties it to the sticky texture the dressing takes on when mixed, and another links it, like the vinegar-miso dressing called "nuta," to the sliminess of a muddy marsh.

sources.title: ぬた芋 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「お茶の葉天ぷら」は、新茶の時期にだけ味わえる宮崎県の郷土料理。摘みたての新芽に薄く衣をつけてさっと揚げ、軽く塩をふって食べる。新芽は柔らかく、お茶の香りとほのかな苦みが持ち味で、新しい芽ほど苦みが穏やかという。新茶の時期、地元でしか味わえない季節限定の味という。温暖な気候に恵まれた宮崎ならではのお茶の楽しみ方でもある。

## どう作るのか
摘みたての新芽を軽く水で洗い、薄く衣をつけてサッと揚げる。揚げたてに軽く塩をふって食べるのが一般的という。使うのは新しい芽から3枚目までで、下にいくほど苦みが強くなるという。新芽ならではの柔らかさと、お茶本来の香りを楽しめる、この時期だけの食べ方という。天ぷら以外の調理法ではあまり見られない、独特の食べ方でもある。

## なぜこの形になったのか
温暖な気候と適度な降雨、肥沃な大地に恵まれた宮崎県は、お茶の栽培に適した土地とされる。古くは山間に自生する山茶を摘んで飲用していたと伝わる。一年で最初に摘む新茶には、飲むと長生きできる、無病息災で過ごせるといった言い伝えがあり、縁起物として喜ばれてきたという。その新茶の新芽をそのまま食べる形として、天ぷらが親しまれてきたと考えられている。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Ocha no ha tempura, a Miyazaki dish available only during the new tea season, deep-fries freshly picked tea leaves in a light batter and serves them with a sprinkle of salt. The tender young leaves carry the aroma of tea with a faint bitterness, milder in the newest leaves, offering a seasonal, locally exclusive flavor found only during the new tea harvest.

## How it's made
Freshly picked tea leaves are rinsed lightly in water, coated in a thin batter, and quickly deep-fried. They're typically eaten fresh from the fryer with a light sprinkle of salt. Only the first three leaves from each new shoot are used, since the lower leaves grow more bitter. It's a way to enjoy the tenderness of new growth and the tea's natural aroma, available only for this brief season.

## Why it took this shape
Miyazaki, blessed with a mild climate, moderate rainfall, and fertile soil, is considered well suited to tea cultivation. In earlier times, people are said to have picked wild mountain tea growing in the hills to brew as a drink. The first tea picked each year carries a tradition that drinking it brings long life and freedom from illness, making it a favored, auspicious harvest. Eating the new leaves directly, in the form of tempura, is thought to have grown out of that same reverence for the season's first tea.

sources.title: お茶の葉天ぷら 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「ざぶ汁」は、人参やごぼう、じゃがいも、大根、かぼちゃなど根菜をたっぷり使う都農町の郷土料理。さまざまな食材を“ざぶざぶ”と煮ることから、この名がついたといわれる。いりこと昆布でとった濃いめの出汁に、根菜の甘みがしっかり溶けこんだ、具だくさんで栄養満点の汁という。練り物を加えて旨味に厚みを出す家庭も多いという。

## どう作るのか
いりこと昆布で濃いめの出汁をとる。野菜は皮をむいて小口切りにし、練り物は薄切りにする。野菜を炒めてから出汁で煮て、砂糖としょうゆで味をととのえ、仕上げにねぎを散らす。入れる具材の数が多いぶん、家にある身近な野菜で代用してつくれるという。具材を大きめに切ると、より食べ応えのある一杯に仕上がるという工夫も伝わっている。

## なぜこの形になったのか
西に尾鈴山、東に日向灘を望む都農町は、日照時間が長く温暖な気候と良質な水に恵まれた農業の町とされる。この土地で育つ根菜や野菜を無駄なく使う日常の家庭料理として「ざぶ汁」が根づいたと伝わる。行事食というより普段の食卓にのぼる料理であり、手に入りやすい野菜でつくれることから、季節を問わず食べられてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Zabu-jiru, a dish from Tsuno town, uses a generous mix of root vegetables such as carrot, burdock, potato, daikon, and pumpkin. Its name is said to come from the "zabu-zabu" sound of the vegetables simmering together. A rich dashi made from dried sardine and kombu carries the sweetness of the root vegetables through, making for a hearty, nutritious soup packed with ingredients.

## How it's made
A rich dashi is made from dried sardine and kombu. Vegetables are peeled and cut into small pieces, and any fish cake is sliced thin. The vegetables are stir-fried, then simmered in the dashi, seasoned with sugar and soy sauce, and finished with a scattering of scallion. With so many ingredients going in, whatever vegetables are on hand at home can usually stand in.

## Why it took this shape
Tsuno, with Mount Osuzu to the west and the Hyuga Sea to the east, is said to be a farming town blessed with long hours of sunshine, a mild climate, and good water. Zabu-jiru is said to have taken root as an everyday home dish built around the root vegetables grown on that land, without waste. More a daily staple than a dish for special occasions, it's said to have been eaten year-round thanks to its reliance on easy-to-find vegetables.

sources.title: ざぶ汁 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「とりめし」は、鶏肉と人参、ごぼう、しいたけなどを炊きこんだ、宮崎県内で広く食べられている炊きこみごはん。稲刈りや畑仕事の合間に、家族が握ってくれたおむすびとして食べられてきた農家飯という。鶏肉の旨味が米一粒一粒にしみこみ、具材の香りが食欲をそそる一皿という。鶏肉をよく食べる土地柄を映した、宮崎らしい炊きこみごはんでもある。

## どう作るのか
細く切った鶏肉を鍋で炒め、だし汁とささがきにした人参、ごぼう、細切りのしいたけなどを加えて調味料で味をととのえ、全体に味をしみこませる。洗い上がった米にこの具材を混ぜ合わせて炊きあげる。大勢が集まるお祭りやイベントでは、大釜で炊いてふるまわれることもあるという。具材を先に煮こんでから米と合わせるため、味が均一に行き渡るという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
鶏肉をよく食べる宮崎県をはじめとする九州地方では、「とりめし」が日常的に親しまれてきたと伝わる。稲刈りや畑仕事の合間、田んぼの畔や畑のかたわらで、家族が握ってくれたおむすびを頬張る光景が各地で見られたという。お祝いの席で振る舞われることも多く、地域や各家庭で味付けや具材に個性が出るのも、この料理が長く親しまれてきた理由という。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Torimeshi is rice cooked with chicken, carrot, burdock, and shiitake, eaten widely across Miyazaki. It's said to have started as a farmer's meal, shaped into rice balls by family members and eaten during breaks from rice harvesting or fieldwork. The chicken's flavor soaks into every grain of rice, and the aroma of the other ingredients rounds out the dish.

## How it's made
Thinly sliced chicken is stir-fried in a pot, then dashi and shaved carrot, burdock, and shredded shiitake are added and seasoned so the flavor soaks through everything. This mixture is combined with washed rice and cooked together. At festivals and gatherings where many people come together, it's sometimes cooked in a large pot and served to everyone.

## Why it took this shape
Across Kyushu, and especially in Miyazaki, where chicken is eaten often, torimeshi is said to have become an everyday favorite. Families are said to have shaped it into rice balls and eaten them along a paddy's edge or beside a field during breaks from harvesting or farm work, a familiar sight across the region. It's also often served at celebrations, and the way seasoning and ingredients vary by area and household is said to be part of why it has stayed beloved for so long.

sources.title: とりめし 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「日向黒皮かぼちゃの煮物」は、宮崎市に伝わる黒く艶やかな皮の黒皮かぼちゃを、砂糖や薄口しょうゆでじっくり煮た料理。西洋かぼちゃとは違うさっぱりとした味わいで、まろやかな甘みときめ細かい舌ざわりが特徴という。皮まで美味しく食べられ、煮崩れしにくいため、煮物にぴったりの品種とされる。βカロテンが豊富で、ビタミン類やカルシウムも含む栄養価の高い野菜という。

## どう作るのか
黒皮かぼちゃを大きめにカットし、砂糖や薄口しょうゆなどの調味料とともにコトコト煮る。煮崩れしにくいため、大きめに切っても形を保ったまま仕上がるという。カレーや味噌汁、おでんに入れて食べる楽しみ方もあり、幅広い料理に活用できるという。甘みが控えめでカロリーも低いため、日々の食卓にも取り入れやすいという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
日照時間が全国でも上位に入る温暖な宮崎県は、たっぷりの日光を浴びて育つ黒皮かぼちゃの産地として知られてきたとされる。支柱につるを這わせて縦にのばす立体栽培という独特の育て方が根づいており、ごつごつとした見た目ながら皮まで美味しく食べられる品種として大切にされてきたという。冬至や煮物などかぼちゃを使う料理に、この黒皮かぼちゃを選ぶ家庭は今も多いという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Hyuga kuro kabocha no nimono simmers Miyazaki's dark-skinned black pumpkin, glossy and nearly black in color, slowly in sugar and light soy sauce. Unlike Western pumpkin, it has a cleaner, lighter flavor, with a mellow sweetness and a fine, smooth texture. Even the skin is good to eat, and because it holds its shape well when simmered, it suits this kind of slow-cooked dish.

## How it's made
The black pumpkin is cut into large pieces and simmered slowly with sugar and light soy sauce. Because it holds together well, it keeps its shape even when cut into large chunks. It also works well stirred into curry, miso soup, or oden, making it a versatile ingredient beyond this one dish.

## Why it took this shape
Miyazaki, with some of the longest hours of sunshine in the country and a mild climate, is known for growing this black-skinned pumpkin under abundant sun. It's grown using a distinctive method of training the vines vertically up a trellis, and despite its bumpy, uneven look, the whole vegetable, skin included, is valued as good to eat. Many households are still said to reach for this black pumpkin specifically for dishes like this one, especially around the winter solstice.

sources.title: 日向黒皮かぼちゃの煮物 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「れんこんのすり流し汁」は、新富町水沼神社ほとりの池でとれるれんこんをすりおろし、だし汁と味噌で仕立てた温かい汁物。独特の歯ごたえと糸を引く粘りが持ち味とされ、地元では親しみをこめて呼び名がついているほどという。冬の寒さに負けない滋養の一杯として大切に受け継がれてきたという。すりおろすことでとろみが出て、体にやさしい口あたりになるという。

## どう作るのか
れんこんは金たわしできれいに洗い、油揚げは油抜きをして細めの短冊に切る。アジ煮干しのだし汁を沸騰しない程度に温め、油揚げを加えたあと、鬼おろしでれんこんをすりおろしながら加える。ひと煮したら溶いた味噌を加え、煮立つ直前に火を止める。仕上げに青ねぎと柚子の皮を添えるという。柚子の香りが加わることで、より奥行きのある味わいになるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
この池のれんこんは、財政の立て直しをめざした藩主が良質な品種を取り寄せ、地元にれんこんの植栽をすすめたことがはじまりと伝わる。空洞に空気を通す構造から、れんこんは“見通しが明るい”“子宝に恵まれる”縁起物とされ、慶事に欠かせない食材になったという。真冬の泥にもぐって収穫する重労働は主に男性の仕事とされ、冬の風物詩として受け継がれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Renkon no surinagashi-jiru is a warm soup made by grating lotus root grown in a pond near Minuma Shrine in Shintomi and mixing it into dashi and miso. The lotus root is known for its distinctive crunch and stringy stickiness, prized enough locally to have earned its own affectionate nickname, and the soup is treasured as a nourishing dish to fend off the winter cold.

## How it's made
The lotus root is scrubbed clean with a metal scrubber, and fried tofu is blanched to remove excess oil and cut into thin strips. Dashi made from dried horse mackerel is warmed just below a boil, the fried tofu added, then the lotus root grated directly into the pot with a coarse grater. After a brief simmer, dissolved miso is stirred in, and the heat is turned off just before it boils. It's finished with a scattering of scallion and yuzu peel.

## Why it took this shape
The lotus grown in this pond is said to trace back to a domain lord who, seeking to shore up struggling finances, brought in a fine variety of lotus root and encouraged locals to cultivate it. Because its hollow chambers let air pass through, lotus root is considered an auspicious food symbolizing clear foresight and fertility, making it essential at celebrations. Harvesting it by wading into the freezing winter mud was reportedly hard labor left mainly to men, and it's said to have become a fixture of the winter season in this area.

sources.title: れんこんのすり流し汁 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「いりこもち」は、炒ったもち米を粉にしてつくる宮崎県全域の郷土菓子。「いり粉」からつくることが名の由来という。香ばしい香りとやさしい甘み、やわらかな食感が特徴で、お盆のお供えやおやつとして親しまれてきた。手軽な材料でつくれる一方、気温や湿度に仕上がりが左右される繊細な菓子でもあるという。見た目は素朴だが、一度食べると記憶に残る味わいという。

## どう作るのか
もち米とうるち米を8対2、あるいは7対3ほどの割合で合わせて炒り、臼でひいて粉にする。砂糖や水、塩を加えてこね、熱湯を加えると生地が徐々にまとまっていき、もちもちとした食感に仕上がるという。白砂糖と黒砂糖のどちらを使うかで風味が変わり、寝かせたあと棒状に切って完成させる。硬くなったら温め直して食べることもできるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
江戸時代から薩摩藩に伝わる節句菓子とされ、子どもの成長を祝って近所に配る風習があったと伝わる。江戸時代中期ごろからは庶民的な菓子として広く親しまれるようになったという。手に入りやすい材料と難しくない手順で、宮崎の気候・風土に根ざしたおやつとして日常的に食べ継がれてきたと伝わる。地域の和菓子屋や直売所でも今なお手づくりのものが並んでいるという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Irikomochi is a confection from across Miyazaki made by toasting glutinous rice and grinding it into flour, which is said to give the sweet its name, from "irikoi," meaning toasted flour. It has a nutty aroma, gentle sweetness, and soft texture, and has long been offered at Obon or enjoyed as a snack. It's simple to make from easy-to-find ingredients, yet a delicate sweet whose result depends on the day's temperature and humidity.

## How it's made
Glutinous rice and ordinary rice, combined at roughly an eight-to-two or seven-to-three ratio, are toasted and ground into flour with a mill. Sugar, water, and salt are worked in, and adding hot water gradually brings the dough together into a soft, chewy texture. Using white or brown sugar changes the flavor, and once rested, the dough is cut into sticks to finish. If it hardens, it can be warmed again before eating.

## Why it took this shape
The sweet is said to date to a festival confection handed down in the old Satsuma domain from the Edo period, given out to neighbors to celebrate a child's growth. From the middle of the Edo period, it's said to have become a widely loved treat among ordinary people. Made from readily available ingredients with a simple method, it's said to have remained an everyday snack rooted in Miyazaki's climate and way of life.

sources.title: いりこもち 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「地鶏の味噌ころばかし」は、小林市など宮崎県西地方に伝わる、地鶏を味噌で煮転がした家庭料理。「ころばかし」とは、この地方の方言で鍋のなかで煮転がすことを意味するという。水を使わずに調理することで、地鶏本来の旨味を閉じこめた濃厚な味わいに仕上がるという。味噌のコクと地鶏の旨味が凝縮された、この地方ならではの味わいという。

## どう作るのか
地鶏を一口大に切り、水を使わずに鍋で煮転がしながら調理する。焦げつかないよう注意を払う必要があり、圧力鍋を使うと早く仕上がるものの、地鶏本来の味が薄れてしまうため避けたほうが良いとされる。こんにゃくや人参、大根、ごぼうを乱切りにしてゆでたものを加えると、より食べ応えのある一皿になるという。家庭ごとに味噌の配合や煮こむ時間が異なるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
霧島山麓一帯には古くから在来種の地鶏が飼育されており、宮崎県内では昔から鶏料理が好んで食べられてきたと伝わる。水を加えずに鍋のなかで煮転がす調理法は、この地方ならではの地鶏の食べ方として受け継がれてきたという。家庭によってつくり方や一緒に入れる具材が異なり、お祝い事や来客のもてなしにも欠かせない料理として親しまれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Jidori no miso korobakashi, handed down in Kobayashi and the western Miyazaki area, is a home-style dish of free-range chicken tossed and simmered in miso. "Korobakashi" is a local dialect word meaning to roll and tumble food in a pot as it cooks. Because it's cooked without added water, it's said to produce a rich flavor that concentrates the chicken's natural taste.

## How it's made
The chicken is cut into bite-sized pieces and cooked in a pot without adding water, tossed and rolled as it simmers. Care is needed to keep it from scorching, and while a pressure cooker speeds things up, it's said to be best avoided since it dulls the chicken's natural flavor. Adding roughly cut, parboiled konjac, carrot, daikon, and burdock makes for a heartier dish.

## Why it took this shape
Native free-range chickens have long been raised around the foot of the Kirishima mountains, and chicken dishes are said to have been a favorite across Miyazaki for a long time. Cooking it by rolling it in a pot without added water is said to have been passed down as a way of preparing chicken unique to this region. Recipes and accompanying ingredients vary by household, and the dish is said to have remained a fixture for celebrations and for entertaining guests.

sources.title: 地鶏の味噌ころばかし 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「酢のしゅい」は、おろした大根とイワシを酢としょうゆで煮た、宮崎県西地方の温かい酢の汁物。「しゅい」は汁を意味するという。なますは冷たいのが一般的だが、こちらは汁物として体を温めるのが特徴で、旬の野菜と酢の酸味を生かした料理という。餅つきの際などにお餅とともに食べられてきたと伝わる。秋から冬にかけてとれる脂ののったイワシを使うと、より美味しく仕上がるという。

## どう作るのか
いりこや昆布で出汁をとり、大根おろしとイワシを加えて酢としょうゆで味をととのえる。イワシはぶつ切りにするほか、しょうがや片栗粉を加えてイワシボールにすることもあるという。魚の旨味が大根おろしにからみ、体がじんわり温まる仕上がりになるという。出汁の濃さや酢の加減は、家庭ごとに好みが分かれ、それぞれの味が受け継がれているという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
酢には殺菌力や疲労回復の効果が古くから知られており、江戸時代に米酢が広く出まわるようになったことで、酢を使った料理が各地に定着していったとされる。都城市では古くから大根が自生しており、その大根を活かす料理として「酢のしゅい」が根づいたともいわれる。寒い日に体を温める工夫として、冬を中心に日常の食卓に並んできたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Su no shui is a warm, vinegared soup from western Miyazaki, made by simmering grated daikon and sardine in vinegar and soy sauce. "Shui" is a local word for soup. While a vinegared salad is usually served cold, this dish is served hot, making the most of seasonal vegetables and vinegar's tang in soup form. It's said to have traditionally been eaten alongside freshly pounded mochi.

## How it's made
Dashi is made from dried sardine and kombu, and grated daikon and sardine are added, seasoned with vinegar and soy sauce. The sardine is sometimes cut into chunks or formed into small balls with ginger and potato starch mixed in. The fish's flavor clings to the grated daikon, and the soup is said to warm the body gently from the inside.

## Why it took this shape
Vinegar has long been known for its antibacterial properties and its effect on recovering from fatigue, and once rice vinegar became widely available in the Edo period, vinegar-based dishes are said to have taken root across the region. Daikon has reportedly grown wild in the Miyakonojo area since long ago, and su no shui is said to have developed partly as a way to make good use of it. As a way to warm the body on a cold day, it's said to have become a regular part of the table, especially through the winter months.

sources.title: 酢のしゅい 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「せりのよごし」は、ゆでて刻んだせりを、豆腐と白ごま、味噌、砂糖をすり合わせた衣で和えた宮崎県内各地の白和え。「よごし」とは白和えのことで、すり鉢やすりこ木を汚しながらつくることからこの名がついたといわれる。せりの爽やかな香りと歯ざわり、鮮やかな緑が持ち味の副菜という。旬の若く柔らかい茎葉を使うと、より風味豊かに仕上がるという。

## どう作るのか
せりはゆですぎないよう10秒ほどさっとゆでるのがコツで、天然のものはアクが強いため下ゆで後しばらく水にさらすとよいという。水気をきった豆腐とごま、味噌、砂糖をすり鉢ですり合わせて和え衣をつくり、ゆでて刻んだせりを加えて和える。淡白な味わいのため、精進料理の一品として法事や仏事にも手づくりされてきたという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
せりは奈良時代にはすでに食用とされていた記録が古い文献に残る、日本原産の野菜とされる。水分の多い土壌を好み、稲刈り後の田んぼやあぜなどにも自生してきたと伝わる。一箇所から競り合うように生えることが名の由来という。豆腐や白ごまで和えることで栄養価を高める、昔の人の知恵が感じられる料理として受け継がれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Seri no yogoshi is a tofu-dressed salad found across Miyazaki, made by tossing boiled and chopped water dropwort, or "seri," in a dressing of mashed tofu, white sesame, miso, and sugar. "Yogoshi" is a local word for this style of tofu dressing, said to come from the way a mortar and pestle get messy in the making. The dish carries seri's refreshing aroma, crisp texture, and vivid green color as a simple side dish.

## How it's made
Seri should be boiled only briefly, about ten seconds, to avoid overcooking, and wild seri, which tends to be more bitter, is best soaked in water for a while after a quick blanch. Drained tofu is mashed together with sesame, miso, and sugar in a mortar to make the dressing, then the boiled, chopped seri is folded in. Because of its plain, clean flavor, it has also been made by hand as part of the meat-free dishes served at Buddhist memorial services.

## Why it took this shape
Seri is a plant native to Japan, recorded as a food in old texts dating back to the Nara period. It favors damp soil and is said to grow wild in rice paddies and along footpaths after the harvest. Its name is said to come from the way it grows in a dense, competing cluster from a single spot. Dressing it with tofu and sesame is said to reflect an old wisdom for boosting the nutritional value of a humble seasonal green.

sources.title: せりのよごし 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「七とこずし」は、旧島津藩の都城地方に伝わる正月の行事食で、大根や人参、ごぼう、白菜、もやし、せり、しいたけなどの野菜に丸もちや米を加えた雑炊。都城地方では雑炊を「ずし」と呼ぶという。一般的な七草がゆとは異なる具だくさんの雑炊で、数え7歳の子どもの成長を願う行事とともに受け継がれてきたという。野菜の旨味が溶けこんだ汁に、もちの食感が加わるのも持ち味という。

## どう作るのか
鍋に大根、人参、ごぼう、里芋、戻したしいたけとだし汁を入れて煮る。炊いたごはんを加えて調味料で味をつけ、もちを入れて柔らかくなったら、もやしとせりを加えて混ぜ合わせ火を止める。近所数軒でつくったこの雑炊を分け合っていただくのが、もともとの習わしだったと伝わる。具材を大きめに切ることで、食べ応えのある一杯に仕上がるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
正月七日は地元で「ななとこさんの日」と呼ばれ、数え7歳の子どもが晴れ着姿で近所を7軒まわり、七草を炊きこんだ雑炊をもらう行事があったと伝わる。子どもの成長と健康を願う特別な一日として、結婚式に匹敵するほど盛大に祝われていたという。現在は神社や寺院でお祓いを受けるかたちで残り、晴れ着姿の子どもたちがお参りする光景も見られるという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Nanatoko-zushi is a New Year's ritual dish handed down in the Miyakonojo region, once part of the old Satsuma domain: a rice porridge loaded with daikon, carrot, burdock, napa cabbage, bean sprouts, water dropwort, and shiitake, along with round mochi and rice. In the local dialect, rice porridge is called "zushi." Unlike the typical seven-herb rice porridge, this hearty, vegetable-packed version is tied to a custom celebrating a child's seventh year.

## How it's made
Daikon, carrot, burdock, taro, and rehydrated shiitake are simmered in dashi in a pot. Cooked rice is added and seasoned, then mochi goes in; once it has softened, bean sprouts and water dropwort are stirred in and the heat is turned off. Traditionally, this porridge was made by several neighboring households and shared among them.

## Why it took this shape
The seventh day of the New Year is locally known as "Nanatoko-san no hi," a day when, tradition holds, a child turning seven by the old counting method dressed in formal clothes and visited seven neighboring homes to receive a bowl of porridge cooked with seven herbs. It's said to have once been celebrated on a scale comparable to a wedding, as a special day wishing for a child's growth and health. Today the custom survives mainly as a blessing received at a shrine or temple, where children in formal dress are still a familiar sight.

sources.title: 七とこずし 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「めの餅あられ」は、小正月の飾り物「めの餅」を1月30日ごろまで飾ったあと、油で揚げてあられにしたお菓子。紅白に黄色や緑を加えたお餅を、小鳥が起きないうちに切りとった榎木の枝に刺して飾ったものという。揚げたてに醤油やきな粉で味をつける、行事とお菓子が一体になった食べ方という。飾り終えた餅を無駄にしない、暮らしの知恵が形になったお菓子でもある。

## どう作るのか
飾り物としての役目を終えたら、榎木の枝からお餅を外し、油で揚げてあられに仕上げる。揚げると小さく膨らみ、餅を煎るときの跳ねる音とともに、空から降る霰に似たかたちになるという。仕上げに醤油やきな粉など、好みの味付けをして食べる。色とりどりのお餅を使うため、揚げあがりも彩り豊かになり、見た目にも楽しめるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
「めの餅飾り」は五穀豊穣や家内安全を願う南九州地方の小正月の伝統行事とされ、語源は「繭のもち」といわれる。繭の豊産を祈ってかたどったのがはじまりと伝わり、厄払いや農作物の豊穣、春の訪れを祝う意味も込められているという。役目を終えた餅を無駄にせずあられに仕立てる工夫が、行事菓子として今に伝わっているという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Meno mochi arare is a sweet made by displaying "meno mochi," small New Year's decorative rice cakes, until around January 30th, then deep-frying them into a crunchy snack. Red, white, yellow, and green mochi were skewered onto a hackberry branch cut before the birds woke, then set out as a decoration. Once taken down, they're fried and seasoned to taste with soy sauce or kinako.

## How it's made
Once the decoration has served its purpose, the mochi pieces are removed from the hackberry branch and deep-fried into a crunchy snack. As they fry, they puff up slightly, and the popping sound and small round shape are said to resemble hailstones, or "arare," falling from the sky. They're finished with a seasoning of choice, such as soy sauce or kinako soybean flour.

## Why it took this shape
The meno mochi decoration is a Koshogatsu, or Little New Year, tradition in the southern Kyushu region, made to pray for a good harvest and a safe household, and its name is said to derive from a word for silkworm cocoons. It's said to have originated as a shape made to wish for a bountiful cocoon harvest, and it's also said to carry meanings of warding off misfortune, wishing for a good crop, and welcoming spring. Turning the mochi into a fried snack once its role as decoration was done is said to be a resourceful way of making sure nothing went to waste.

sources.title: めの餅あられ 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「おび天」は、日南市飫肥地区に伝わる魚肉練り製品で、揚げかまぼこの一種。イワシやアジ、サバなど日向灘でとれる大衆魚をすり身にし、豆腐を混ぜて味噌や黒砂糖で味付けして揚げる。豆腐が入るぶん薩摩揚げよりやわらかくふわりとした食感で、少し甘めの独特な味わいという。二次加工をせず揚げたてをそのまま食べるのが一般的という。

## どう作るのか
魚をおろして骨を取り、軽くたたいてから水気を切った豆腐とすり鉢でする。しょうがや溶き卵、調味料を加えてさらによくすり、好みのかたちに整えて油で揚げる。常温でも美味しいが、揚げたては黒砂糖の甘みが際立ち、おやつ代わりにも食べられるという。使う魚の種類によっても風味が変わるため、店ごとに個性が出るという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
江戸時代、飫肥藩領の領民たちによって考え出されたと伝わる料理という。もともと飫肥周辺では味噌を使う料理が多く、サトウキビ栽培が広まったことを背景に、味噌と黒砂糖を組み合わせた「おび天」が生まれたと考えられている。田植えや稲刈り、運動会など日常のさまざまな場面で食べられ、庶民の味として飫肥地区に根づいていったという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Obiten is a fish-paste product from the Obi district of Nichinan, a type of deep-fried kamaboko. Common fish caught in the nearby Hyuga Sea, such as sardine, horse mackerel, and mackerel, are ground into a paste, mixed with tofu, seasoned with miso and brown sugar, and deep-fried. The tofu gives it a softer, fluffier texture than satsuma-age fish cake, along with a distinctive, slightly sweet flavor. It's typically eaten straight from the fryer without further cooking.

## How it's made
The fish is filleted and deboned, lightly pounded, then ground together with drained tofu in a mortar. Ginger, beaten egg, and seasonings are worked in thoroughly, and the mixture is shaped as desired before deep-frying. It's good at room temperature too, but fresh from the fryer, the brown sugar's sweetness stands out, making it something people also enjoy as a snack.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to have been devised by residents of the Obi domain during the Edo period. Miso-based cooking was already common around Obi, and against the backdrop of sugarcane cultivation spreading through the area, this combination of miso and brown sugar is thought to have given rise to obiten. Eaten on occasions ranging from rice planting and harvesting to school sports days, it's said to have taken root in the Obi district as an everyday food for ordinary people.

sources.title: おび天 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

items.body_ja:
## 何でできているか
「かに巻き汁」は、宮崎県南部の北郷町に伝わる、秋から冬にかけてとれる「山太郎ガニ」（モクズガニ）を丸ごとすりつぶしてつくる味噌仕立ての汁物。味噌がカニの旨味を包みこむことから、この名がついたといわれる。澄んだ汁に浮かぶふわふわとした食感のなかに、カニの旨味が凝縮された一杯という。秋の訪れとともに味わう、この地域ならではの季節の恵みという。

## どう作るのか
生きた山太郎ガニをよく洗い、甲羅を外してミキサーなどで細かく砕きつぶす。水と味噌を加えて混ぜ、ざるでこして鍋に入れる。弱火でゆっくり熱を加えると、カニのたんぱく質と味噌の成分が反応し、おぼろ豆腐のように固まっていくという。器に盛り、おろししょうがやねぎを添える。そうめんやうどんを加えても美味しいという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
山太郎ガニは海で生まれ、川を上って成長したあと産卵のために海へ下るため、その時期を狙って漁がおこなわれると伝わる。この地域にとって貴重なたんぱく源であり、ゆでて食べても美味しいカニをまるごとすりつぶすことで、旨味を余すことなく引き出す知恵が生まれたという。秋になると地域の人々が心待ちにする、季節を告げる一品として親しまれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Kanimaki-jiru, from Kitago in southern Miyazaki, is a miso-based soup made by grinding whole "santaro-gani" river crab, caught from autumn into winter, and mixing it into a miso broth. The name is said to come from the way the miso wraps the crab's flavor into the soup. Suspended in a clear broth, the soft, cloud-like texture of the crab carries a concentrated burst of flavor.

## How it's made
Live santaro-gani crabs are washed well, their shells removed, then ground fine in a blender or similar tool. Water and miso are mixed in, and the mixture is strained through a sieve into a pot. Heated slowly over low heat, the crab's protein reacts with the miso and sets into something like soft tofu curds. It's served in a bowl with grated ginger and scallion, and somen or udon noodles can be added for a heartier meal.

## Why it took this shape
Santaro-gani crabs are born at sea, grow as they climb upriver, then head back down to the sea to spawn, and this is said to be the season targeted for the catch. As a valuable source of protein in this area, grinding the whole crab, one that's also good boiled and eaten, is said to have developed as a way to draw out every bit of its flavor without waste. It's remained a beloved dish that people in the area are said to look forward to each autumn, a taste that announces the changing season.

sources.title: かに巻き汁 宮崎県｜うちの郷土料理：農林水産省

## 何でできているか
「ねりくり」は、蒸したさつまいも（甘藷）とゆでた餅をすり鉢でつき混ぜ、きな粉をまぶした都城市の郷土菓子。地域によって「ねったぼ」「ねったくり」「からいも餅」とも呼ばれるという。さつまいもの自然な甘みと餅のもちもちした食感が合わさり、素朴でやさしい味わいという。中に小豆あんを忍ばせることもあり、味わいに変化をつけられるという。

## どう作るのか
蒸し上がった甘藷と餅をすり鉢で丁寧につき混ぜる。甘藷と餅の割合はおよそ3対1が良いとされる。かたちよく丸めるか適当な大きさにちぎり、きな粉をまぶして食べる。甘藷を蒸す途中で市販の切り餅を上にのせて一緒に蒸し、柔らかくなったらつき混ぜる方法もあるという。中に小豆あんを入れることもあり、家庭で手軽につくれる菓子という。

## なぜこの形になったのか
江戸時代からつくられてきたとされ、正月の餅つきの際、最後の一臼に煮た甘藷を加えてつきあげたのがはじまりと伝わる。「ねりくり」とは宮崎弁で“つきまぜる”という意味といわれる。正月に余って硬くなった餅を無駄にせず使う工夫として広まり、主食の代わりや農作業の合間の間食としても食べられてきたという。さつまいもは大陸から伝わったことから「からいも」とも呼ばれてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Nerikuri, a confection from Miyakonojo, is made by pounding steamed sweet potato and boiled mochi together in a mortar and dusting the result with kinako soybean flour. In some areas it's known by other names, such as "nettabo," "nettakuri," or "karaimo-mochi." The natural sweetness of the sweet potato meets the chewy texture of the mochi for a simple, gentle flavor, and sweet red bean paste is sometimes tucked inside for variety.

## How it's made
Steamed sweet potato and mochi are pounded and mixed together carefully in a mortar, ideally at a ratio of about three parts sweet potato to one part mochi. The mixture is shaped into balls or torn into pieces by hand, then dusted with kinako. One method steams a store-bought rice cake on top of the sweet potato as it steams, then pounds the two together once softened. Sweet red bean paste is sometimes tucked inside as well, and it's a confection easy enough to make at home.

## Why it took this shape
The dish is said to date back to the Edo period, originating when the last batch of a New Year's mochi-pounding session was made by pounding boiled sweet potato in along with the rice. "Nerikuri" is said to mean "pound and mix" in the local dialect. It's said to have spread as a way to use up mochi that had hardened after the New Year without waste, and it has also been eaten as a substitute for a meal or a snack during breaks from farm work. Sweet potato is also said to be called "karaimo," reflecting its arrival in Japan from the Asian continent.

## 何でできているか
「つわぶきの油炒め」は、あく抜きしたつわぶきを油揚げなどと炒め、しょうゆや砂糖で味付けした日南地方の家庭料理。つわぶきはキク科の多年草で、ふきに似るが常緑性で一年中青々としており、厚みのある葉に光沢があるのが特徴という。ほろ苦さとシャキッとした歯ごたえが持ち味の、素朴な副菜という。旬の若葉を使うと、より柔らかく食べやすいという。

## どう作るのか
つわぶきは皮をむいて水にさらし、あく抜きをする。たっぷりの湯に塩を入れてゆでたあと、よく炒めて油揚げなどを加え、しょうゆや砂糖で味をととのえる。ほろ苦さが特徴のため、あく抜きの加減が味の決め手になるという。日常のおかずとして食卓にのぼることが多い一品で、常備菜として多めにつくり置く家庭もあるという。

## なぜこの形になったのか
つわぶきは日本原産の植物で、九州地方など一部地域で古くから食用にされてきたとされる。温暖な気候の宮崎県南部の沿岸地帯には、海岸線に沿って自生してきたと伝わる。日南地方では毒消しの作用があるとも伝えられ、佃煮や和え物などさまざまな調理法とともに、油炒めも庶民的な食べ方として親しまれてきたという。春先に若葉が出るこの時期を旬として、家庭で日常的に食べられてきたという。
items.body_en:
## What it's made of
Tsuwabuki no aburaitame is a home-style dish from the Nichinan area, made by stir-frying tsuwabuki, or Japanese silverleaf, with fried tofu and seasoning it with soy sauce and sugar after removing its bitterness. Tsuwabuki is a perennial in the daisy family, resembling butterbur but evergreen year-round, with thick, glossy leaves. It offers a simple side dish with a mild bitterness and a crisp, satisfying bite, milder and more tender when made from young spring leaves.

## How it's made
Tsuwabuki is peeled and soaked in water to draw out its bitterness. It's boiled in plenty of salted water, then stir-fried well and combined with fried tofu, seasoned with soy sauce and sugar. Because its character comes from that mild bitterness, how thoroughly it's soaked beforehand is said to make the difference in flavor. It's a dish that often appears as an everyday side on the table, and some households make a larger batch to keep on hand.

## Why it took this shape
Tsuwabuki is a plant native to Japan, said to have been eaten in parts of Kyushu since long ago. It's said to grow wild along the coastline of southern Miyazaki's mild coastal areas. In the Nichinan area, it's also said to have been valued for a detoxifying effect, and alongside preparations like simmered tsukudani or dressed salads, this stir-fry is said to have remained a familiar, everyday way to eat it, especially in early spring when the young leaves first appear.
